differences.title: 1. ARCHITECTURE STYLE
differences.leftDesc: NATS JetStream uses a publish-subscribe model with persistent streams, allowing clients to pull or receive pushed messages, optimized for high throughput and low latency.
differences.rightDesc: RabbitMQ implements AMQP, offering flexible routing via exchanges and queues. Consumers explicitly bind to queues to receive messages, enabling complex message delivery patterns.

differences.title: 2. PERSISTENCE MECHANISM
differences.leftDesc: JetStream stores messages in an append-only, replayable log. This enables efficient storage, deduplication, and retrieval of message history for stream processing.
differences.rightDesc: RabbitMQ stores messages in queues, which can be durable. Messages are typically removed upon acknowledgment by a consumer, making them ephemeral by default.

differences.title: 3. DEPLOYMENT SIMPLICITY
differences.leftDesc: NATS is distributed as a single, lightweight binary, making deployment and scaling exceptionally simple across various environments, including edge and cloud.
differences.rightDesc: RabbitMQ typically requires multiple components (broker, management plugin) and careful configuration, especially for clustering and high availability setups.

differences.title: 4. CONSUMER MODEL
differences.leftDesc: JetStream supports durable consumer subscriptions that track their progress in the stream, allowing for seamless reconnections and guaranteed message redelivery.
differences.rightDesc: RabbitMQ can have exclusive consumers that are the only ones to receive messages from a queue, or shared consumers that load-balance messages.

differences.title: 5. LATENCY & THROUGHPUT
differences.leftDesc: NATS is designed for extreme performance with sub-millisecond latency and high throughput, leveraging efficient protocols and in-memory processing where possible.
differences.rightDesc: RabbitMQ offers good performance but generally has higher latency due to its feature set and protocol overhead, suitable for many enterprise use cases.

differences.title: 6. DATA MODEL
differences.leftDesc: JetStream abstracts persistence through 'Streams' (logs) and 'Consumers' (subscription points), simplifying stream management and replayability for event-driven architectures.
differences.rightDesc: RabbitMQ uses 'Exchanges' for routing and 'Queues' for message storage, providing a versatile but more explicit model for message distribution.

differences.title: 7. CLOUD NATIVE
differences.leftDesc: NATS JetStream is built with cloud-native principles, excelling in containerized environments, Kubernetes, and distributed systems, prioritizing simplicity and resilience.
differences.rightDesc: RabbitMQ is a mature, feature-rich broker widely used in enterprise, but its cloud-native story is often achieved through additional orchestration and tooling.
